chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us from Salama ibn al-Khattab al-Birawustani, from Ibrahim ibn Muqatil. He said: Hamid ibn Muhammad narrated to me from 'Amr ibn Harun, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all). He said:

I had intended to marry Fatima, daughter of Muhammad (blessings of Allah upon them both), for a period, but I did not dare mention it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). That longing stirred in my chest night and day, until I visited the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said: O Ali! I said: I am at your service, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Are you interested in marriage? I said: The Messenger of Allah knows best. I thought he intended to marry me to one of the women of Quraysh, and I was afraid of losing Fatima. I had not noticed anything, when the messenger of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came to me and said: Answer the Prophet and hurry — we have never seen the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) more joyful than today. He said: So I hurried to him, and he was in the chamber of Umm Salama. When he looked at me, his face lit up with joy and he smiled, until I saw his white teeth gleaming. He said: Rejoice, O Ali! For indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has relieved me

of the concern I had about your marriage. I said: How is that, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Gabriel came to me with spikenard and cloves from Paradise and presented them to me. I took them and smelled them, then said: What is the reason for this spikenard and cloves? He said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commanded the angelic inhabitants of the Gardens and all that was therein to adorn all the Gardens with their plantations, trees, fruits, and palaces; and He commanded their winds to blow with all kinds of perfumes and fragrances; and He commanded their houris to recite therein Surah Ta-Ha, the Ta-Sins, Ya-Sin, and Ha-Mim-'Ayn-Sin-Qaf. Then a caller called from beneath the Throne: Verily! Today is the day of the wedding feast of Ali ibn Abi Talib! Verily! I take you as witnesses that I have married Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, to Ali ibn Abi Talib by My own will — each of them for the other. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent a white cloud that rained upon them its pearls, emeralds, and rubies. The angels stood and scattered the spikenard and cloves of Paradise — this is from what the angels scattered. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, commanded an angel from the angels of Paradise named Rahil — and there is none among the angels more eloquent than him — and said: Give a sermon, O Rahil! And he delivered a sermon the like of which the people of

The herald then called out: 'Verily, O My angels and dwellers of My Garden, bestow blessings upon Ali ibn Abi Talib, the beloved of Muhammad, and Fatima the daughter of Muhammad, for I have already bestowed My blessing upon them both. Verily I have married the most beloved of women to Me to the most beloved of men to Me after the prophets and the messengers.' Angel Rahil said: 'O my Lord, is not Your blessing upon them both greater than what we have seen for them in Your gardens and Your abode?' Allah the Mighty and Majestic then said: 'O Rahil, verily among My blessings upon them both is that I will unite them both in My love, and I will make them both a proof over My creation. By My might and My majesty, I will certainly create from them both a creation, and I will certainly raise from them both a progeny whom I will make My treasurers on My earth, and mines of My knowledge, and callers to My religion — through them I will establish My proof over My creation after the prophets and the messengers.' So rejoice, O Ali, for Allah the Mighty and Majestic has honored you with an honor the like of which no one has been honored, and I have married you to my daughter Fatima according to what the Most Merciful has married you, and I am pleased for her with what Allah is pleased for her. So take your wife, for you are more worthy of her than I, and indeed Gabriel has informed me...

...that Paradise is longing for you both, and were it not that Allah the Mighty and Majestic had decreed that from you both would emerge what He would take as a proof over the creation, Paradise and its inhabitants would have surely responded (1) for your sake. What an excellent brother you are, and what an excellent son-in-law you are, and what an excellent companion you are — and it suffices you that the pleasure of Allah is your pleasure.' Ali (peace be upon him) said: I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, has my station reached such a point that I was truly mentioned in Paradise, and Allah married me among His angels!' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily when Allah the Mighty and Majestic honors His intimate friend and loves him, He honors him with what no eye has seen nor ear has heard, and Allah has bestowed it upon you, O Ali.' Ali (peace be upon him) then said: '(My Lord, inspire me to give thanks for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me)' (3), then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah send blessings upon him and his family) said: 'Amen' (4).

key_terms.حُجَّة: Proof/Argument — the divinely appointed authority whose obedience is incumbent on all creation; a key theological concept in Shia Islam
key_terms.خَتَن: Son-in-law/groom — referring to the marriage relationship with the Prophet
key_terms.خُزَّان: Treasuries/keepers — referring to the Imams as custodians of divine knowledge
key_terms.سُنْبُل: Spikenard — an aromatic plant from Paradise used as a symbol of divine blessing
key_terms.قَرَنْفُل: Cloves — a fragrant spice associated here with Paradise's flora
key_terms.مَعَادِن: Mines/sources — metaphor for the Imams as wellsprings of divine knowledge
key_terms.وَلِيمَة: Wedding feast, the celebratory banquet marking a marriage

ai.seo_question: How was the marriage of Imam Ali and Sayyida Fatima celebrated in Paradise according to hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the celestial marriage of Imam Ali (AS) and Sayyida Fatima (AS) as recounted by Imam Ali himself through a chain traced to Imam al-Sadiq. The narrative describes how Allah decreed their union in Paradise, commanding the angels to adorn the Gardens, sending Gabriel with flowers, and announcing the marriage from beneath the Divine Throne. The hadith highlights the divine election of their progeny as Proofs (Hujjas) over creation, emphasizing that their children would serve as treasuries of divine knowledge and callers to religion after the prophets.
